# Antcluster — distilled knowledge (from website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is
**Antcluster** (antcluster.com) is an **"AI Native Data Agent | Enterprise Data Nervous System"** built on a **self-constructed Enterprise Knowledge Graph (EKG)**. Its H1 is **"Enterprise data nervous system"** with subhead: **"AI Native Data Agent Built on a knowledge graph. Skip the ETL. Deploy analytics, reporting, and machine learning agents in natural language."**

## Core value (one-liners per audience)
- **Enterprise data/analytics leader:** "Skip the ETL. Ask natural language questions; get SQL, research, and analysis grounded in your data graph — read-only, non-invasive, enterprise-ready."
- **IT/architecture:** "Graph-centric approach (EKG + Ontology Builder) that self-repairs on schema changes and compounds over time; zero data movement; queries at source."
- **Business user:** "AI-native data agent that investigates, not just translates — three layers, one verified answer."

## How it works (3 layers)
1. **Layer 1 — Graph-Centric Context Engine**: builds/maintains Enterprise Knowledge Graph; Topology maps how data behaves; self-repairs on schema changes; Ontology Builder closes gaps. "Builds the map. Fills its own gaps."
2. **Layer 2 — Planner-Orchestrator**: plans before querying (decomposes into contract), delegates, routes evidence, resolves conflicts; conversational memory layer. "Plans before it queries."
3. **Layer 3 — Agent Swarm**: five specialists (SQL, Python, ML, NLP, Report) with debate/conflict resolution; commits to closest defensible answer. "When interpretations conflict, the swarm debates. When evidence is thin, it asks for more. It commits only to the closest defensible answer — not the fastest one."

## Swarm specialists
- **SQL** — generates & validates SQL across dialects
- **Python** — stats, transformations & data analysis
- **ML** — auto-selects best-fit ML model at runtime
- **NLP** — text extract, sentiment, entity recognition
- **Report** — compiles findings into formatted reports + charts

## Database connectivity
Connects to relational databases: **PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, ClickHouse**.

## Enterprise/security (stated)
- **Zero Data Movement (ZDM)** — never writes to databases; queries at source; no ETL pipeline; no data copies created; read-only connector; permissions beyond read not granted.
- **Deployment** (referenced as DEPLOY layer)
- **RBAC**
- **Audit**
- Taglines: "Read-only · Non-invasive · Enterprise-ready."

## Industries (examples)
- **Manufacturing:** OEE trend for Line 4 across shifts excluding planned maintenance (ERP/MES/QMS/PLM/SCADA context)
- **FMCG:** SKU-level margin variance by channel adjusted for trade spend (SAP, distributor portals, trade promotion systems)
- **Automotive:** defect rates across supplier batches last 6 months by plant/component (quality records, supplier data, production logs)
- **Energy:** assets degrading fastest and generation revenue at risk over next quarter (SCADA, CMMS, asset registers, weather feeds)

## CTAs / nav
- **Try it Yourself → https://app.antcluster.com**
- **See How It Works → #about**
- **Book a Demo → /book-demo**
- Nav: Overview (/), Architecture (/architecture: EKG/AntHive/AntSwarm), Enterprise (/enterprise), Solutions, Resources.

## Contact
- **Email:** info@antcluster.com
- **Website:** https://antcluster.com/

## Notes
As of 2026-10-19, site emphasizes graph-centric approach, self-repair on schema changes, planning before querying, swarm debate, zero data movement. Specific pricing not stated in captured materials.

# Antcluster — distilled knowledge (from website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is
**Antcluster** (antcluster.com) is an **"AI Native Data Agent | Enterprise Data Nervous System"** built on a **self-constructed Enterprise Knowledge Graph (EKG)**. Its H1 is **"Enterprise data nervous system"** with subhead: **"AI Native Data Agent Built on a knowledge graph. Skip the ETL. Deploy analytics, reporting, and machine learning agents in natural language."**

## Core value (one-liners per audience)
- **Enterprise data/analytics leader:** "Skip the ETL. Ask natural language questions; get SQL, research, and analysis grounded in your data graph — read-only, non-invasive, enterprise-ready."
- **IT/architecture:** "Graph-centric approach (EKG + Ontology Builder) that self-repairs on schema changes and compounds over time; zero data movement; queries at source."
- **Business user:** "AI-native data agent that investigates, not just translates — three layers, one verified answer."

## How it works (3 layers)
1. **Layer 1 — Graph-Centric Context Engine**: builds/maintains Enterprise Knowledge Graph; Topology maps how data behaves; self-repairs on schema changes; Ontology Builder closes gaps. "Builds the map. Fills its own gaps."
2. **Layer 2 — Planner-Orchestrator**: plans before querying (decomposes into contract), delegates, routes evidence, resolves conflicts; conversational memory layer. "Plans before it queries."
3. **Layer 3 — Agent Swarm**: five specialists (SQL, Python, ML, NLP, Report) with debate/conflict resolution; commits to closest defensible answer. "When interpretations conflict, the swarm debates. When evidence is thin, it asks for more. It commits only to the closest defensible answer — not the fastest one."

## Swarm specialists
- **SQL** — generates & validates SQL across dialects
- **Python** — stats, transformations & data analysis
- **ML** — auto-selects best-fit ML model at runtime
- **NLP** — text extract, sentiment, entity recognition
- **Report** — compiles findings into formatted reports + charts

## Database connectivity
Connects to relational databases: **PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, ClickHouse**.

## Enterprise/security (stated)
- **Zero Data Movement (ZDM)** — never writes to databases; queries at source; no ETL pipeline; no data copies created; read-only connector; permissions beyond read not granted.
- **Deployment** (referenced as DEPLOY layer)
- **RBAC**
- **Audit**
- Taglines: "Read-only · Non-invasive · Enterprise-ready."

## Industries (examples)
- **Manufacturing:** OEE trend for Line 4 across shifts excluding planned maintenance (ERP/MES/QMS/PLM/SCADA context)
- **FMCG:** SKU-level margin variance by channel adjusted for trade spend (SAP, distributor portals, trade promotion systems)
- **Automotive:** defect rates across supplier batches last 6 months by plant/component (quality records, supplier data, production logs)
- **Energy:** assets degrading fastest and generation revenue at risk over next quarter (SCADA, CMMS, asset registers, weather feeds)

## CTAs / nav
- **Try it Yourself → https://app.antcluster.com**
- **See How It Works → #about**
- **Book a Demo → /book-demo**
- Nav: Overview (/), Architecture (/architecture: EKG/AntHive/AntSwarm), Enterprise (/enterprise), Solutions, Resources.

## Contact
- **Email:** info@antcluster.com
- **Website:** https://antcluster.com/

## Notes
As of 2026-10-19, site emphasizes graph-centric approach, self-repair on schema changes, planning before querying, swarm debate, zero data movement. Specific pricing not stated in captured materials.

# Archer Development Foundation — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**Archer Development Foundation is a nonprofit organization in formation that is drafting OASIS — the Open Agent Systems Interoperability Standard: an open interface so AI agents can discover specialized services, act with bounded permission, and carry attributable evidence of what happened — without being locked to one platform.** The site labels everything a working draft: "OASIS-0001 · v0.1-DRAFT", "Proposed architecture. No ratified standard or deployed network is implied."

**One line per audience:**
- Researchers/providers: "A public technical brief and an open research agenda on evidence, concurrency and offchain effects."
- Independent implementers/integrators: "An interface anyone can implement — conformance vectors and licensing terms still to be published."
- Institutions/sponsors: "A consortium now forming (Founding/Contributing/Supporting tiers), standing earned, governance proposed."

## How it works (the model, as proposed)
- **Problem the site states:** today an agent's access to a service depends on an operator's catalog, credentials, invocation conventions and private history; open client code alone doesn't remove that.
- **The six-stage conceptual lifecycle:** Discover → Verify → Route → Authorize → Consume → Attest (ServiceDescriptor → InvocationRequest → InvocationEnvelope → Delegation & consent → EffectReport → ExecutionReceipt/RecordUpdate; OASIS-0008 FeedbackEvidence is OPEN/informative).
- **One response, four independent concerns:** data · cost · authorizations[] · record.
- **Topology (proposed):** principal+agent → chosen indexer (signed descriptors) → compatible executor (policy/quote/invocation) → service adapter (provider logic/credentials) → external systems; optional registry/evidence chain anchors references, not raw credentials.
- **Design sequence:** first provider-hosted adapters (portable contracts with existing endpoints), later network-hosted workers (to be evaluated).
- **Payments:** rail-neutral profiles — flat-stablecoin profile in the first repo proposal; x402 compatibility needs a separate profile; cards via Stripe MPP Shared Payment Tokens as a candidate extension. "Signing or submitting a transaction does not establish finality or service delivery."

## Key figures (site, as of 2026-10-19)
- Status: **OASIS-0001 · v0.1-DRAFT · OPEN SPECIFICATION** (working draft, not ratified).
- Message contracts in the brief: OASIS-0002–0007 core, OASIS-0008 (FeedbackEvidence) informative/open.
- **4 design objectives** (identity that travels; catalog anyone can rebuild; execution with choice; history you can carry).
- **6 open research questions** (Q.01–Q.06: evidence/reputation, concurrency & shared budgets, offchain effects after ambiguous timeouts, availability & privacy, network economics, ongoing authority after invocation).
- **Proposed milestones:** 2026 make the contract explicit · 2027 demonstrate independence · 2028 evaluate/build coordination harness · 2029 groundwork for an open node network. The charter states: "Years express goals, not delivery commitments."
- Consortium: **3 proposed membership tiers** (Founding, Contributing, Supporting); **3 ways to participate** (Foundation team member, consortium member, integrator).
- Timeline page: Web1 (readable) → Web2 (platform) → Web3 (ownable) → Web4 (agentic, explicitly "a possible next chapter / proposed", not a settled era).

## Audiences and what each gets
### Researchers, service providers, institutions
- Public technical brief (/standard) and proposed charter (/charter) are discussion documents; the foundation invites counterexamples, threat models, test cases and reproducible experiments.

# ARF AI — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**ARF AI is a governance and reliability control plane that sits between autonomous AI agents and enterprise infrastructure: before a governed write action runs, deterministic policy gates, an explainable risk score and (where required) a human approval decide whether it proceeds — and every decision is recorded in a signed, tamper-evident audit trail.** Actions ARF cannot model are refused outright ("zero upstream calls"). Storage/ONTAP operations first. Current release label on the site: **v4.3.2 — Axiom** (as of 2026-10-19).

**One line per audience:**
- Platform/SRE leads: "You decide what AI tooling may do in production — ARF enforces that decision, not just documents it."
- Founders/CTOs with nobody to delegate to: "When a customer's security review asks who governs your agents' actions, the answer is something you can show, not describe."
- Teams adopting AI-driven operations: "The speed of autonomous AI, with the ability to explain in writing what happened and why."

## How it works (7-step pipeline from the site)
1. **Application** — any client, any request shape.
2. **LLM / AI agent** — non-deterministic reasoning (probabilistic).
3. **Policies** — matched to tenant rules (ARF control plane).
4. **Risk engine** — explainable scoring (site shows example score 0.31).
5. **Approval** — deterministic gate (the agent cannot approve its own request; an approval admits exactly the call it was given for).
6. **Execution** — runs only once cleared.
7. **Audit trail** — signed, hash-chained, tamper-evident; editing any entry afterwards makes the chain fail verification.

**Recorded demo (simulated ONTAP cluster):** an agent asks to delete production volume `app_data` → ARF records the attempt before anything runs → the delete is held until a storage admin approves → the approval names `app_data` only, so deleting another volume waits again → after approval the delete runs and an independent read confirms the volume is gone → an unmodeled delete (`delete_lun`) is refused with zero upstream calls.

## Key figures (site, as of 2026-10-19)
- Version: **v4.3.2 — Axiom**.
- Free sandbox: **1,000 evaluations/month**, mock responses, no agreement required.
- Pilot snapshot: **free · 3 founding slots**, in exchange for a written reference.
- Write-access review: **$4,500 fixed** for one agent (card or invoice).
- 4 capability subsystems · 7 architecture steps · SOC 2: criteria mapped to control and code, **"Not yet audited."**
- Response commitment: "We reply within two business days."
- Terms of Service effective **October 2, 2026**; AI chat logs retained 30 days; pilot signup data up to 12 months.
- The site states: "No customer quotes or numbers appear here until they are real."

## Four capability subsystems ("Four subsystems, one control plane")
| # | Subsystem | What it does (site) |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | Policy Enforcement | Deterministic execution gates, approval workflows, regional policy controls, cost guardrails |
| 02 | Decision Governance | Audit trail of every governed decision, cryptographic attestation, attribution & accountability, PDF audit report export |
| 03 | Continuous Reliability | Anomaly detection, predictive health scoring, control-theoretic stability monitoring, Lyapunov-guided stabilising actions |
| 04 | Operational Transparency | Explainable risk scores, counterfactual what-if analysis, live Prometheus metrics, causal attribution |

## Three properties a compliance officer asks for (site: "a mechanism, not a policy document")
- **Tamper-evident audit trail** — recorded, timestamped, attributed (including the action proposed alongside the one that ran); anyone holding an export can verify integrity.
- **Mechanical enforcement** — on a governed write path, gates cannot be silently overridden; every override is recorded with its approver.
- **Explainable reasoning** — every risk score comes with its inputs: the prior, the evidence, and the expected loss of allowing, denying or escalating. "Never a black box."

## Three access models (pricing page)
| | Sandbox | Pilot snapshot | Write-access review |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | Free, no agreement | Free · 3 founding slots | **$4,500** fixed, card or invoice |
| What you get | Simulated decisions | Five-tool write-access map | Map of every write path in the agreed tool inventory + recoverability + scored history + gap list |
| What they need | Synthetic or redacted payloads | Tool list + representative traces | Tool definitions + action history |
| Access to your systems | None | Read-only material only | Read-only material only |
| Enforcement | Simulated only | None — analysis only | None in the review; a gate is by invitation afterwards |
| Support | Community | Founder-led | Founder-led |
After a review, **a continuous gate is available by invitation**, scoped and priced per engagement. "Nothing automatic. No subscription starts and nothing else is billed."

## Positioning / objections (site's own answers)
- **"Is this real / audited?"** SOC 2 trust-services criteria are mapped to the control and code — **"Not yet audited."** No customer quotes or numbers are shown "until they are real."
- **"Is the sandbox production-grade?"** No — "returns simulated responses only… treat it as a demonstration surface," use synthetic or redacted payloads. Terms: sandbox API returns mock data only, rate-limited, "as is", not suitable for production.
- **"Is the engine open source?"** No — "The core engine is proprietary — no public license is granted." The public agentic-reliability-framework code on GitHub is not the ARF engine; the public specification is shared under written terms, not open source.
- **"Is this instead of evaluation/adoption?"** "ARF is built for the step after evaluation, not instead of it."
- **"Why now?"** Autonomous AI is moving from copilots to autonomous workflows; as AI acts rather than recommends, organisations need infrastructure that governs execution, manages operational risk and provides auditability by design.
- **"Why not just use an LLM/agent?"** "Foundation models are probabilistic. Enterprise operations require deterministic control. ARF bridges that gap."
- **"Which agents is this for?"** Teams whose agents move from read-only recommendations to production changes — infrastructure and storage first; other consequential changes (e.g. customer-facing commitments) can be scoped on a call.
- **Regulated answer:** "You may not be the regulated enterprise — your customer is, and their security review is the deadline." Sectors: financial services, healthcare, government & defence, critical infrastructure, enterprise AI platforms.

## Specifics for answers
- Pricing: only the three published tiers; continuous gate "by invitation, scoped and priced per engagement" — never invent a price for it.
- Sandbox API example: `POST https://arf-ai-arf-sandbox-api.hf.space/v1/evaluate` with JSON `{"service_name":"api","event_type":"latency","severity":"high","metrics":{"latency_ms":450}}`.
- Specs (Core Governance Engine, API Control Plane, Enterprise Layer, Enterprise Specification) are "pilot only" — request via /signup.
- Signup form: 3 steps (about you → technical details → budget & terms); fields include industry, role, company size, HQ. Work email used only for pilot coordination — "no mailing lists, no spam."
- Privacy: data may be processed in the US (Standard Contractual Clauses); no sale of personal data; demo hosted on Hugging Face (mock data only).
- FAQ page lists 15 question headings (general, usage, performance & limitations, engagement & licensing) but the answers are rendered client-side and were not captured in the crawl — do not invent answers; direct to juan@arf-ai.com.

## Contacts
- juan@arf-ai.com (on every page) · Book a call: https://calendly.com/petter2025us/30min · LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/agentic-reliability
- Slack community (invite link in footer) · GitHub: https://github.com/arf-foundation · Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/ARF-AI · Risk demo: https://arf-foundation.github.io/arf-risk-demo/
- Pilot request: https://arf-ai.com/signup ("The founder replies personally, with no commitment required.")
- Per the founder's intro in the Connectors WhatsApp group — not stated on the site: Juan Petter.

# Audacious AF — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**Audacious AF (branded "Audacious AI Friends") is an in-person New York City community for women leaders who are building, or starting to build, with AI — hands-on workshops, salon-style discussions, skill shares and meetups in intentionally small rooms.** Founded in 2026 by Maggie Blackburn, Paige Kehoe and Samantha Provenza. Events run on Luma (luma.com/audaciousaf); the community site is audaciousaf.com. Its stated mission: "Closing the AI gender gap one skillshare, workshop and meetup at a time."

**One line per audience:**
- Member/attendee: "Small, hands-on NYC rooms where you can talk about what excites, scares and overwhelms you about AI — without explaining your background first."
- Partner/sponsor: "The women in our rooms are changing how their companies work with AI. Get in the room with them — no sales pitches."
- Host: "Open your office or studio for a workshop — Wi-Fi, a screen, and room for laptops is all we need."

## How it works
1. **Discover** — events listed on audaciousaf.com/events and luma.com/audaciousaf.
2. **Register on Luma** — free RSVP, paid ticket, or approval-required ("Request to Join"); some locations hidden until you register.
3. **Show up IRL** — mostly in person in NYC, some virtual; workshops are laptop-open, "you leave having made something."
4. **Membership (coming)** — join the waitlist at audaciousaf.com/join; applications open → founding cohort admitted. "Founding membership is coming" — no price published.
5. **Partner** — host a night, sponsor, put a product in the room, send a speaker, offer a member perk, or run a series (three sponsorship levels).

## Key figures (audaciousaf.com, as of 2026-10-19)
- **150+ IRL members · 1,300+ community members · 8+ events held since June 2026 · 5+ company partners.**
- Role breakdown (by members' job titles): Founder 22% · C-suite & VP 10% · Director/Head 12% · Manager 19% · IC Builders 36% — "45% are founders, C-suite, or director level and above."
- Corporations worked with: **Anthropic, Webflow, Live Nation, Pinterest, Wayo.**
- Members & attendees from: Vercel, Stripe, Squarespace, Google, PayPal, Airbnb, Bloomberg, Capital One, Cursor.
- Upcoming events on 2026-10-19: **6** (1 meetup, 1 panel, 4 workshops & trainings). Past list on /community shows **11 events Jun–Oct 2026**.
- Free "Build with AI" meetups drew large counts on Luma: +265 interested / 270 going (Oct 13), +90 / 95 going (panel), +50 / 67 going (hackathon weekend).

## Event formats (site: "How we connect and learn")
- **Connect** — meetups, small groups, "more dinners and socials on the way."
- **Learn** — panels and skill shares ("hear from women doing the work, and trade what you know").
- **Build** — workshops & trainings, hands-on, laptop open.
- **Co-workshop format (2× monthly):** 8:30–9:00 breakfast · 9:00–10:00 workshop/build · 10:00–10:30 Q&A · 10:30am–5pm optional coworking. Tickets include breakfast; bring a laptop.

## Current event lineup (from audaciousaf.com/events, as of 2026-10-19)

# Bicameral — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**Bicameral is a decision-recall and decision-governance layer for lean software teams working with AI — "the GitHub of Decisions."** It pulls decision context from the team's tools (tickets, docs, meeting notes, agent sessions), connects each decision to the code it governs, keeps a human-reviewed ledger of what was approved/superseded, and runs an advisory "preflight" that surfaces relevant past decisions — and conflicts — before new work starts. Today: **private alpha, local-first, human-reviewed**; it is not generally available.

**One line per audience:**
- Founder/CTO/eng leader: "A source of truth for decisions, so context stops getting lost in Slack and the same argument doesn't get relitigated."
- PM/engineering pair: "Recall and conflict checking in MCP — past decisions and contradictions surfaced before code is written."
- AI-agent user: "Human stays between evidence and authority — nothing enters the ledger automatically."

## How it works (4 steps, from /how-it-works)
1. **Bring in evidence** — a ticket, document, meeting note or agent session explaining what the team is trying to do.
2. **Connect it to the code** — show where the decision applies so the context is useful at the next implementation.
3. **Human review** — a person accepts, rejects or supersedes the candidate. **"Nothing becomes part of the ledger automatically."**
4. **Recall before coding** — advisory preflight returns the relevant decision, its source and its code references before work continues.

**Today:** local-first, human-reviewed — decision capture, code grounding, auditable ledger, advisory preflight (MCP).
**Next (being built, not shipped):** shared context across the team, live integrations (Slack, Linear), coding-agent host paths, drift detection.

## Key figures (site, as of 2026-10-19)
- **Featured on Hacker News — 193 points, 147 comments** (badge on the homepage; item 46866481).
- **Bicameral developer survey: 40+ responses (2026).** Findings: **35%** of technical-constraint communication leaves no persistent record; **52%** share constraints via copy-paste to Slack; **25%** mention them verbally with no written record; ~**one-third** of constraints are already in a product conversation; **~50%** are discovered only during implementation; **70%** of constraints need to reach people who don't regularly interact with the codebase.
- Blog: **7 posts**, Feb 2 – Aug 8, 2026 (authors: Jin Kuan, Leon Schwarzer).
- Alpha fit: team size **21–50 marked "(best fit)"** on the application form.
- Third-party stats the blog cites (attribute as "Bicameral cites…"): Index.dev 2025 (21% more tasks completed, no company-wide delivery improvement), METR 2025 (experienced devs 19% slower yet believed faster), Apiiro 2024 (48% of AI-generated code contains security vulnerabilities), IDC 2024 (only 16% of developer time writing code), Atlassian 2025 (~10 hours/week saved by assistants, largely cancelled out).

## The problem it names (homepage)
**"Communication is the new bottleneck."** Decision fatigue, 4 steps: an idea gets pitched → it gets lost in Slack → it gets lost in the cracks → when you need the result it isn't ready. "The decision gets reconstructed until the original context is gone."
Working example on the site: ticket **PAY-2847** ("Add retry for failed payments") conflicts with approved decision **PAY-1192** ("No automatic retries — customer re-submits payment", approved by Marco (eng), source Notion/ADR-0014, 2026-03-23) → the bicameral bot flags the conflict → "Supersede earlier decision" → "PAY-1192 superseded — recorded to the decision ledger."

## Product pieces shown on the site
- **Agent preflight** in the terminal: "bicameral preflight · 4 decisions on file · Payments" with context and PM notes (e.g. "Priya · PM note on PAY-2847 · 2026-06-20").
- **Controlled corpus:** "Maintains an evidence-backed list of specification decisions, surfacing potential conflicts before they are admitted to the canonical ledger."
- **Curate in the loop:** fetches source candidates from every integration at implementation time, then tracks the promoted ones as governing constraints.
- **Decision card detail:** status (proposed/approved), sources (e.g. `fathom://may-21-risk-review 00:23:47` with a quoted line), governed files (`kyc/review_queue.ts:71-94`), and explicit conflicts ("Overlaps with 'Manual review queue for failed auto-verify' · Marco (eng) · 2026-03-23") with Accept/Reject.
- **Trust model:** "Trust the process, not just the model… a human stays between evidence and authority — before anything becomes part of the ledger." Ungoverned "faulty path" is shown as the alternative that produces conflicting fallback policies.

## Research thesis (blog — the "why")
- **Feb 2, 2026 "Coding assistants are solving the wrong problem"** (Jin Kuan; the HN post): coding assistants bury requirement gaps instead of escalating them; tech debt "is created in product meetings" — deadlines, scope cuts, "ship now, optimize later."
- **Feb 9, 2026 "Why 'just prompt better' doesn't work"**: survey findings above; "AI speeds up implementation but bypasses the very process through which constraints were discovered."
- **Aug 8, 2026 "The Context Laundering Problem"** — "Context management is not a technical problem, it is an authority problem": context passing through customer → brief → Linear → GitHub → agents can be fused into a coherent-looking spec that "smuggles provisional guesses into the mix alongside binding constraints." Their fix borrows from finance KYC: attribute context at the point it enters the system, maintain a review queue separating proposed from binding decisions — "an upstream human provenance layer — who said what, carried across agent sessions." Also cites two Claude Opus 4.8 failure reports as why "unsolicited cleverness" in models is a problem ("when the model invents a product decision, who is held accountable?").
- Company belief: formal-verification techniques applied to spec checking and fast recall; "turn AI from a sycophantic coworker into a predictable tool developers can trust."

## Positioning / objections
- **"Is it another code-analysis/docs tool?"** No — "what is needed is not another code analysis or documentation tool, but ammunition to drive cross-functional alignment upstream."
- **"Will it auto-approve decisions?"** No — human review is mandatory; "Today that means a human stays between evidence and authority."
- **"Is it GA / can I buy it?"** No — private alpha; "See whether Bicameral fits your team." No pricing page exists.
- **"Does it replace my tools?"** No — evidence comes *from* Notion/Linear/Slack/git and lands in the ledger; those integrations are the "next" step.
- **Humans vs AI:** "Why We Bet on Humans" (Apr 28, 2026) — "Human intelligence will always remain king"; the tooling exists so "human developers with their superior ability to creatively problem-solve will always come up on top."

## Specifics for answers
- Alpha application (/waitlist): work email, role (Founder/CTO/VP Engineering/Engineering manager/Other), team size (1–5 / 6–20 / **21–50 (best fit)** / 51–150 / 151+), optional "Where does decision context get lost?". "We'll use your response to understand fit and follow up personally."
- Contact (/contact): form with problem categories; anonymous option; direct email jin@bicameral-ai.com.
- Community: Google Group groups.google.com/g/bicameral — "we would especially appreciate help in architecting our agent harness."
- Privacy page (/privacy) is largely a Google OAuth `drive.file` scope transparency doc: what flows where, what the company can/cannot see as OAuth app publisher, local data, telemetry, contact section.
- Legal entity: **Bicameral AI, Inc.** © 2026. Footer: "team governance layer for AI-accelerated software development."

## Contacts
- support@bicameral-ai.com (every page) · hello@bicameral-ai.com (alpha) · jin@bicameral-ai.com (contact page)
- Apply: www.bicameral-ai.com/waitlist · Contact: www.bicameral-ai.com/contact · Blog: www.bicameral-ai.com/blog · HN: news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46866481
- Per the founder's intro in the Connectors WhatsApp group — not stated on the site: Lovis Axon (LinkedIn lovisaxon/).

# Biobase — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**Biobase (Biobase, Inc.) is a governed network between the systems that hold clinical data — EHR, LIS, PACS, biobanks, billing — and the researchers who need it: one platform, two sides, with the data staying where it lives.** Health systems, labs and biobanks put their archives to work on their own terms; pharma, biotech and AI teams specify a cohort in plain language and get feasibility in minutes instead of a six-month broker cycle. Self-positioning: "We're not another data marketplace. We're the rails that power precision medicine." Mission: "make clinical data accessible across the healthcare value chain, so that data generated in the course of care can accelerate the medicine that follows it."

**One line per audience:**
- Pharma / biotech / AI buyer: "Describe the cohort you need in plain language, see feasibility across the network without any data changing hands, and receive normalized, linked, research-ready data or specimens."
- Health system / lab / biobank supplier: "The most valuable dataset in medicine is already yours — we turn what you hold into revenue through a governed, federated marketplace, on your terms, with custody kept where it belongs."
- Candidate: "Small AI-native team (remote US) building the rails for precision medicine — Claude Code every day, no ticket queue."

## How it works
1. **Describe the cohort** — natural-language intent or precise criteria (indication, stage, specimen, molecular markers); request at biobase.ai/request?intent=data|images|specimens.
2. **Feasibility across the network** — counts and attributes from participating institutions, without data changing hands.
3. **Order with governance built in** — IRB, BAAs and de-identification handled in the workflow; "agents move the process; humans approve the consequential steps."
4. **Receive research-ready data** — normalized, linked, quality-checked, fully traceable; physical specimens or digital datasets.
- Platform's four functions: **Normalizes** (HL7, FHIR, VCF, DICOM, LIMS exports, flat files → OMOP, CDISC, FHIR), **Unifies** (pathology, imaging, molecular, outcomes linked at patient level, across institutions, without data leaving home), **Indexes** (discoverable by research intent, not by knowing which server it sits on), **Bridges** (governed, compliant access between holders and researchers).
- Supplier side: institution keeps custody; de-identification, lineage and audit trails are "enforced by the pipeline itself"; zero-lift onboarding to existing systems; named account ownership and defined response SLAs.

## Key figures (biobase.ai/platform, as displayed 2026-10-19)

# BlockConvey — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**Block Convey, Inc. builds PRISM — a reliability layer for AI apps that finds failures before users do: "Proof your agents work."** You describe what your AI should do, PRISM generates the users you never tested for, runs against your real app, and turns each failure into a re-runnable test and a fix you can validate. Core thesis: "A request can return 200 OK and still fail the user" — an average over everything hides the two things your AI does badly behind the six it does well. Founded on the direction "from visibility to improvement" (it began with AI governance and observability). Free plan with 100 credits/month; company © 2026, pre-launch polish (privacy/terms still "in legal review").

**One line per audience:**
- Builder/developer: "Connect one AI app on the free plan, find the first thing worth improving — 100 credits a month, no card."
- Production team: "Guardrails, evaluators and end-user intelligence on top of full traces — every failure ends with an owner, a date, and a human sign-off."
- Enterprise/regulated: "Evidence mapped to EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001 and more — plus the AI Reliability Program: connect, baseline, review, prioritize, validate, report."

## How it works (the loop)
1. **Understand** — describe what the AI should do.
2. **Generate** — Synthetic Scenarios (Beta) create realistic users, changing requests, missing details, tool problems and edge cases ("Six people your agent has not met yet": intent persistence, slot filling, error handling, ambiguity, tone resilience, knowledge gap).
3. **Run** — connect your app (PRISM SDK, standard OpenTelemetry, LangChain/LangGraph, imports, or API; OpenAI/Gemini proxies at prism.blockconvey.com/proxy/...).
4. **Find** — traces, sessions, agent runs, retrieval, tools, timing, retries, scores, final result in one view (AI Observability).
5. **Diagnose** — Agent Intelligence clusters failures across all sessions (classified on every session, not a sample); AI Remediation brings user goal, actual outcome, trace and likely cause together: "User changed intent at 00:03… What to fix: confirm latest intent before processing irreversible actions."
6. **Prove** — Evaluators re-run the check; the fix is validated on the same cohort that found the problem; monthly artefact = score + deltas + report. "PRISM never merges on its own" — knowledge/guardrail changes in-platform, prompt changes as versioned diffs, code changes as PRs, all requiring explicit human sign-off.

## Platform — six capabilities (/prism)
| Capability | Tagline | Plan gate |
|---|---|---|
| Synthetic Scenarios | "Scenarios you never thought to test" | Beta, all plans (credits) |
| AI Observability | "Every step the agent took, in one view" | all plans |
| Agent Intelligence | "See what your AI keeps getting wrong" | all plans |
| Evaluators | "Quality as a check you can run again" | Builder+ |
| AI Remediation | "From failure to a clear next step" | all plans |
| End User Intelligence | "What users asked that nobody answered" | Growth+ |
- Positioning hook: "Your agent has a score, and the score is lying to you" — PRISM's score has six weighted dimensions (task success 25%, correctness 20%, guardrails 20%, user friction 15%, stability 10%, improvement velocity 10%), "fixed per client, stated in every report," Green at 85.
- "The unit of analysis… is a session, with what the user wanted still attached to what they got" — coverage is "100% of production sessions rather than a sample."

## Pricing (blockconvey.com/pricing, as of 2026-10-19)
| Plan | $/mo | Credits | Traces/mo | Retention | Members | Notable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 100 | 10,000 | 14 days | 1 | core platform, all connectors, KB (50 docs), community support |
| Builder (most popular) | $20 | 400 | 100,000 | 90 days | 5 | + Guardrails (PII/PHI/prompt-injection/regex/off-topic, Monitor+Enforce), Evaluators Hub, human review queue, priority support |
| Growth | $50 | 1,000 | 250,000 | 180 days | 10 | + End User Management, User Risk Profiles, longer audit history |
| Scale | $300 | 4,000 | 1,000,000 | 365 days | 25 | + dedicated Slack, guided onboarding & architecture review, industry scoring (fintech/healthcare/legal) |
| Enterprise | contracted | in agreement | custom | custom | custom | + SSO/SCIM (when available), private deployment, data residency, dedicated infra, custom connectors, contractual SLAs, AI Reliability Program |
- Credit mechanics: one shared balance for all AI-powered actions; PRISM shows action cost + balance before every action; **no automatic overage or plan change** — at zero credits new AI actions pause and existing results stay readable; monthly credits reset, purchased credits persist; failed jobs release reserved credits; top-up minimum 100 credits for $10.
- "Exact limits are confirmed at signup and in the order form." **Compliance reporting is not part of any plan** — a service, on request, scoped before work starts.

## Solutions (/solutions — four paths)
- **For Builders:** "From working demo to real-user ready" — test what you didn't try, connect without rebuilding, see what broke and what to fix first; full core product free before you pay.
- **AI Agents:** "The tool call returned 200. The task still failed." — test the whole run, find the step that changed the result, keep the failure as a test.
- **Conversational AI:** "Turn four is where conversations break" — people don't follow a script; catch the turn where context is lost; measure outcome, not wording.
- **RAG Applications:** "Know whether retrieval or generation failed" — find missing knowledge, separate retrieval vs generation failure, re-run the same question after the fix.

## Enterprise, compliance, security
- **AI Reliability Program** (Enterprise): recurring flow Connect → Baseline → Review → Prioritize → Validate → Report; six deliverables (platform access, guided setup + architecture review, reliability baseline, recurring technical review, priorititized remediation backlog, quarterly executive reliability report); for customer-facing AI in production, high-impact/regulated workflows, and leadership asking for quality/risk/ROI; starts with one important workflow; "does not make changes to production automatically."
- **Compliance** (/compliance): "Evidence, not certification" — PRISM records what the AI did and why; reports map stored evidence to frameworks as a **service on request**: EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, SR 11-7, NY DFS Part 500, NAIC Model Bulletin, CFPB/Reg B, HIPAA, GDPR, DORA, SOX, PCI DSS (12 framework pages linked). New frameworks "added through sponsored development: the first customer who needs one funds it." Trust Packs and human-reviewed, attested reports. Every plan records underlying evidence from day one.
- **Security** (/security): data path — user/app and AI workflow = customer; PRISM connection path = shared; processing/storage/dashboard = Block Convey. Collects only "what the product needs to explain a failure": prompts/responses when configured, session/trace IDs, model metadata, tool calls when supplied, retrieval context, timing/token/cost/errors, eval/guardrail/remediation results, user IDs "only as configured by the customer." Hosted by default; private deployment/dedicated infra/data residency on contract (Enterprise).
- **Legal status (honest gap):** Privacy Policy, Terms and the subprocessor list all state they are "in legal review ahead of the PRISM launch — contact us and we'll send the current copy." Compliance certifications are explicitly NOT offered ("Does this certify us? No.").

## Sample numbers (illustrative — never quote as customer results)
PRISM's own pages show a "sample FinVault reliability report. Design-partner data, synthetic and illustrative": reliability score 78/100 (+6 vs May), failure rate 8.4% (was 12.7%), 48,210 sessions → 4,050 failures clustered → 14 backlog items → 9 fixes proposed → 7 human-approved → 5 shipped & validated; "~$9,700/month measurable value against $5,000/month program cost — ~1.9×"; escalations 9.2%→7.6% (≈771 avoided, ~154 support hours, ~$5,400); ~48 engineering hours saved (~$4,300). The site's footnotes call these "placeholder loaded rates, measured effects only."

## Company, resources, contacts
- **Team (about page):** Arun Prasad — CEO · Aishwarya Birla — CTO · Pavan Marisetti — COO. "Titles are current public information. Full bios are being finalised." Spoken at: NYU AI Conference 2024, Venture Studios Summit 2024.
- **Beliefs:** real outcomes matter (final user result > clean API response); builders need clear next steps (a score isn't enough); "Trust starts with evidence."
- **Resources:** Docs (74KB — integration brief: choose path → instrument → verify → report, API contract, data controls, account limits, failure modes); Guides — 12 titles listed, **all "Coming soon"**; Blog — **"No posts published yet"**; Glossary — "Definitions are being published."
- **Contact:** /contact form exists but **"The form is not connected yet. Email us directly and we will reply from the same address" → arunprasad@blockconvey.com** (only email on the site). Self-serve: /signup (Full Name, Email, Password, Company Name) → free plan; sign in at prism.blockconvey.com/login. Socials: LinkedIn (block-convey-inc), X @blockconvey, Instagram, Threads.
- **CSV contacts (not site channels):** WhatsApp 229020608258273@lid "Pavan" (= COO Pavan Marisetti); LinkedIn post link (Pavan's "I killed founder-led sales" post).

## For answers
- Pricing → quote the five-plan table verbatim with "as of 2026-10-19"; stress free is real ("connect a real AI app… before you pay"), no auto-overage, credits not access.
- Beta/coming-soon honesty: Synthetic Scenarios = Beta; MLflow + tracing platforms + database imports = coming soon/beta; guides/blog/glossary/legal docs = pending — say so plainly.
- Never present FinVault/sample metrics as customer proof; say "the site's illustrative design-partner sample."
- Compliance questions → "evidence, not certification," service on request, 12 supported frameworks.

# Boop.me — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
- **For organizers:** "The event app without the app" — registration/ticketing on your own domain, agenda and calendar invites, QR check-in and badge printing, curated matchmaking, SMS updates, post-event sponsor reporting: "sell the seats, book the meetings, prove the room worked."
- **For exhibitors/sales teams:** QR-to-SMS lead capture that books the meeting before the visitor leaves the booth — "they capture leads, we book meetings." Talking point: "lead capture fills your CRM. Boop fills your calendar."
- **For attendees/individuals:** scan someone's QR, their contact card arrives by text (.vcf), meetings book inside the SMS thread — free to start, no app needed on either side.

## How it works (the core flow)
1. Visitor scans a QR (booth, badge, or personal) → their native Messages app opens with a pre-written SMS, one tap to send (US codes go to **+1 866 395 7922**; UK number and WhatsApp option exist).
2. Boop replies in the thread: sends the contact card (.vcf), asks qualifying questions (custom flow per QR/rep), offers real slots read live from the rep's Google/Outlook calendar.
3. Prospect replies with a number → booking written to the rep's calendar, invite sent to both (Google Meet/Zoom link auto-added); SMS reminders at 24h and 30 min.
4. Contact auto-enriches (email or LinkedIn URL → title, company, industry), syncs to CRM (HubSpot automatic, Salesforce one-click Leads, Zoho; CSV/webhooks anytime).
5. Everything runs over the cellular network — no app install, no venue wifi, works offline for QR/SMS.

## Key figures (per boop.me, as of 2026-10-19)
- **MATCH HOUSE case study (flagship):** SXSW founder-investor event with fireside chat by Bill Gurley (Benchmark) — **$6B+ investor capital represented, 280+ companies, 150+ verified investors, 1,200+ meetings booked before doors** across two MATCH HOUSE events.
- **Curotec case study:** Silicon Slopes, 20,000 attendees → **15 follow-up meetings with qualified executives**; pre-event attendee analysis, executive ski day, QR-to-SMS qualification.

- vs competitors (boop-vs-competitors): Popl (badge scanning/digital cards), Blinq (card exchange), Dot (NFC personal cards), Bitly (links, "not a direct competitor") — Boop's edge = meeting booking in the SMS thread, works on bad wifi, no training needed; blog also compares vs iCapture/atEvent/momencio (tablet-form, app-required).

# BrandKnight — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**BrandKnight is a MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) violation monitoring tool for brands sold through resellers — currently in private beta with a waitlist.** It scans product listings across marketplaces around the clock, catches sellers who break your pricing policy, and produces timestamped evidence you can use for enforcement.

**One line for different audiences:**
- Brand / manufacturer: "24/7 MAP monitoring across 30+ marketplaces, with timestamped evidence instead of manual checks."
- Brand protection team: "Automated scanning + daily violation digests + analytics on repeat violators."
- Note: the site targets companies that sell through others (resellers/retailers); it is pre-launch — you can only join the waitlist.

## How it works (3 steps)
1. **Connect your products** — import your product catalog and define your MAP pricing policies.
2. **We monitor 24/7** — automated scanners check major marketplaces for pricing violations around the clock.
3. **Take action** — get timestamped evidence packages and enforce your pricing policy.

## Key figures (website, as of 2026-10-19)
These are counters displayed in the landing page's illustrative dashboard (marketing demo data — treat them as product claims/illustrations, not audited customer stats):
- Marketplaces monitored: **30+** · Evidence generation: **<60s** · Monitoring: **24/7** · Timestamped evidence: **100%**.
- Dashboard illustration: "5,000+ products scanned", "50+ violations detected", "80 sellers tracked", "$2.4M saved from MAP violations this quarter", "3 violations this week, down from 12 last week".
- Status: **Private Beta** ("We'll notify you at launch. No spam, ever."). © 2026 BrandKnight, Inc.

## Audiences and what each gets
### Brand / company (client)
- Continuous automated scanning of listings on Amazon, eBay, Walmart and 30+ marketplaces.
- Evidence capture: timestamped screenshots of every violation with full page context ("irrefutable proof for retailer conversations").
- Daily reports: a digest of all violations delivered to your inbox; shareable/exportable for enforcement.
- Analytics dashboard: trends, repeat violators, enforcement effectiveness.

### Brand protection / legal teams
- Multi-marketplace coverage in one place; enterprise security claimed: **SOC 2 compliant, encrypted data storage, SSO integration**.

## Positioning / objections
- **Vs manual checking:** the pitch is "Stop chasing violations. Start enforcing pricing." — scanning runs 24/7 instead of you checking by hand.
- **Vs generic monitoring:** BrandKnight frames itself around MAP enforcement specifically (evidence packages for retailer conversations), not general brand protection.
- Honest caveat: everything on the site is pre-launch marketing for a private beta; there is no public pricing, no customer list, and no product screenshots beyond the illustrative dashboard.

## Specifics for answers
- Pricing: **not published** — the only CTA is "Join the waitlist" (email field). Early access + "exclusive pricing" promised at launch.
- No mobile app, no integrations list, no API mentioned on the site.
- Site footer: "MAP violation monitoring for brands that care about pricing integrity. Protect your revenue across every marketplace." Powered by Arcanus (arcanus.com).
- The site is a single-page app: /about, /pricing, /features etc. all serve the same landing page — do not cite them as separate pages.
- Per the Connectors CSV: poster Srdjan Vranac, first posted 2026-09-03; WhatsApp contact "Vranac"; LinkedIn vranac/ — not stated on the site itself.

- No email or phone on the site — only the waitlist form ("Join the waitlist") on brandknight.com.
- Founder contact (per the Connectors WhatsApp group CSV, not stated on the site): WhatsApp "Vranac" (175758819512441@lid), LinkedIn vranac/.

# Chronos — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**Chronos (chronos.ro, by Chronos Labs) is an AI-native GTM (go-to-market) platform — "Your AI GTM Team" — that automates outbound sales for founders and sales teams.** You paste your website; Chronos builds a "GTM digital twin" of your company, then sources leads from a 350M-lead database, writes personalized messages in your voice and runs multi-channel campaigns (LinkedIn, email, SMS, X, Instagram, Facebook, Reddit, Substack, AgentMail) — with pipeline and deal intelligence on top. Founded 2024, HQ San Francisco; the site claims it is VC backed and "Backed by Sam Altman".

**One line for different audiences:**
- Founder: "Paste your website and every outbound channel runs on autopilot, in your voice."
- Sales team / SDR lead: "Outbound intelligence + pipeline mastery + deal coaching you command in plain English; plug in any AI agent via MCP."
- Enterprise: "Managed GTM deployment with SSO, advanced controls and security/procurement review."

## How it works (4 steps, per /info)
1. **Paste your website** — no setup calls; Chronos reads your site, learns product, tone, ICP and differentiators.
2. **It builds your GTM digital twin** — messaging, audience targeting and channel strategy configured within minutes, calibrated to sound like you.
3. **Channels get spun up** — fresh warmed email domains provisioned; LinkedIn, X, AgentMail, SMS, Instagram, Facebook run in parallel from one paste.
4. **Campaigns run themselves** — identifies ideal customers from the 350M-lead database, writes personalized messages, sends recommended daily volume per channel, paced for deliverability.

## Key figures (site claims, as of 2026-10-19 crawl)
- Traction (/info): **3,000+ companies**, **5 enterprise customers** (managing **$30B+** assets), **350M** verified leads, **1M+** messages sent, **$30B+** pipe managed. (Homepage says 3,000+ companies; /about says "1,000+" — cite the page you use.)
- Founded **2024** · HQ **San Francisco, CA** · company: **Chronos Labs** (© 2026).
- Signup: "Unlimited credits. 7 days free on every new account. No charge at signup."
- Affiliate program: **30% of every sale**, paid via Stripe, withdraw anytime.
- Changelog highlights (2026): Browser App launch Mar 8; credits system + Outlook integration Apr 1; AI CMO + mobile responsiveness Apr 8; Deep Research + Apollo migration Apr 13.

## Audiences and what each gets

### Founders (primary)
- "Drop your website and we'll automate your entire GTM." Free browser app to start ($0), no card required.
- Geo Agent finds your ICP, researches every buyer, runs outreach in plain English.

### Sales teams / SDRs
- "Managed GTM" plan: outbound intelligence setup, pipeline mastery workflows, deal coaching configuration, CRM and sales-stack planning.
- Multi-channel orchestration on one ICP; recommended daily send volumes; LinkedIn connection campaigns with rate-limit handling; 5 tone levels (very casual → executive formal).
- Plug any AI agent into your account via **MCP** ("Claude Code for GTM").

### Enterprise
- Custom deployment: team deployment support, advanced workflow controls, security and procurement review, custom onboarding; SSO; invite-code login at app.chronos.ro/enterprise.

## Product surface
- **Platforms:** Desktop app for macOS (v23 — the site currently shows a "Coming Soon / not ready yet" notice pointing users to the browser app), Browser app at app.chronos.ro ("Live · Newest"), iOS app in TestFlight (waitlist), Enterprise (invite code).
- **Channels named:** LinkedIn, Email (Gmail / Outlook / AgentMail), SMS, Twitter/X, AgentMail, Instagram, Facebook, Reddit, Substack.
- **Data providers:** Apollo + Lusha + Prospeo; Deep Research per contact (employment history, education, funding, tech stack, revenue).
- **Integrations page:** Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach, Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator ("availability can vary by account, onboarding plan, and customer stack").
- **Inbox/ops:** replies flow to an inbox with optional automated follow-ups; sequence attachments (PDFs); mini sequences; daily campaign report emails.

## Positioning / objections
- **Vs traditional sales tools** (site's framing): they price around one narrow category (CRM, sequencing, enrichment, conversation intelligence); Chronos is positioned as an AI-powered GTM platform — evaluate the combined outbound + pipeline + deal workflow.
- **Vs "AI bolted onto legacy tools":** "We don't bolt AI onto legacy tools. Every feature is designed from the ground up to be powered by artificial intelligence." Values: AI-native, revenue-first ("deals closed"), founder-built.
- **Vision thesis** ("Consciousness for Companies"): GTM as a living model/synapse of how the company actually sells; full write-up on the founder's Substack. Quote: "Expertise is a movie, not a paragraph" (Nadav Shanun).
- If a message can't be personalized concretely, the site says Chronos **pauses the campaign rather than send something generic**.

## Specifics for answers
- **Pricing:** Browser App **$0 to start** (Pro plan available later, free trial); Managed GTM and Enterprise are **custom** — book a demo. Never invent amounts for paid tiers.
- **Demo:** calendly.com/nadav-geodo/30min (Book Demo); /demos page has a brand film + YouTube tutorial (youtu.be/-9YtWYJ0_PA).
- **Founder:** Nadav Shanun, CEO & Founder (LinkedIn nadavshanun, X @Cookiesarefunnn); founding team background claimed: NASA, CIA, Y Combinator, Entrepreneurs First, Johns Hopkins, MIT, Pentagon/DoD nuclear warheads, The Residency.
- **Support:** "A real person, every time" — phone +1 (561) 431-1345, email nadav@chronos.ro.
- Legal: Terms & Privacy effective March 2026; data on Supabase; site uses reverse-IP visitor identification (company-level only, 90-day retention).
- Hiring: /team page — SWE, GTM, design, PM, video editors; internships/full-time; NYC or SF office fly-outs; cal.com/nadav-shanun-ltsfl5/15min.

- nadav@chronos.ro (email / Contact Us) · +1 (561) 431-1345 (support phone) · Book demo: calendly.com/nadav-geodo/30min · Careers: cal.com/nadav-shanun-ltsfl5/15min

# CopilotResume — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**CopilotResume (copilotresume.io) is an EU-hosted AI resume & CV builder with job tailoring, ATS checks and a job tracker.** You build a resume free (all templates), scan it against a real job ad for an ATS score and missing keywords, get an honest "should I apply?" verdict and a recruiter's-eye read, and export a PDF — first PDF export free. Made by a small Dutch company (ETLDataCompany B.V., Den Haag).

**One line for different audiences:**
- Job seeker: "Build free, get an ATS score against the real job ad, fix weak bullets with AI, track every application — first PDF free."
- Non-native English speakers / international seekers: data stored in the EU, never sold, never used to train AI; toolkit in 16 languages; country-specific formats (Canada, Germany, India, Netherlands, Philippines, South Africa…).
- Coaches / recruiters: site has dedicated pages (/resume-builder-for-coaches, /resume-builder-for-recruiters — linked, not in crawl).

## How it works (4 tools + tracker)
1. **ATS Check** — scores your resume against the real job ad, lists matched and missing keywords.
2. **Verdict** — honest "should I apply?" answer: strengths, gaps, what to do next.
3. **Darpan** — how a recruiter sees your CV: first impression, red flags, what you're worth.
4. **AI Coach** — rewrites a weak bullet into a result-driven one, in your own words and language.
Plus **Job Tracker** (free board): one row per job next to the exact resume used, ATS score saved with it, stages Applying → Interview prep, dated interviews/notes, outcome (offer / rejected / ghosted).
User paths on the homepage: "Ready for a change?" / "Chasing a dream job?" (ATS Check & Verdict → fix with AI Coach) / "Not sure what's going wrong?" (Darpan) / "Want feedback from someone you know?" (Share Live Resume + comments).
Free ATS scan flow: import resume (PDF/DOCX/TXT, "Stored in the EU · never used to train AI") → add job description → scan.

## Key figures (site, as of 2026-10-19)
- **Trustpilot: 4.2/5** — "a small Dutch company, so we don't have thousands of reviews yet — just 6 people who took the time" (3 reviews quoted on site).
- Resume examples library: **31 resume examples** by job title (heavy on AI roles: AI Engineer, AI Product Manager, ML Engineer, Prompt Engineer, AI Red Teamer… plus classic roles: Software Engineer, Data Engineer, DevOps, Product Manager, Sales Director, Registered Nurse, Midwife…).
- Free plan: up to **99 resumes**, all templates, AI Assistant (OpenAI-advanced), AI Coach, and 1 each/month of ATS Check, Verdict, Darpan, Fix with AI.
- Premium: up to 99 active resumes + 99 cover letters, **15 of each** of ATS Check / Verdict / Darpan / Fix with AI **per day**, unlimited imports & PDF exports, Live Resume, Fair View (gender-neutral resume).
- Company: ETLDataCompany B.V., Den Haag, Netherlands · KVK: 87585413 · BTW: NL864338880B01.

## Pricing (site, EUR/USD as displayed)
- **Free** — $0: build, all templates, first PDF export free; AI Coach & Darpan; 1×/month ATS Check, Verdict, Darpan, Fix with AI.
- **Premium** — subscribe **$12/month** (renews monthly, cancel anytime) **or** pay once: **$7 for 1 day** / **for 30 days** (24h or 30 days of full access, nothing to cancel). Features identical between subscribe and pay-once.
- Refund: email within 3 days of charge, if you haven't downloaded a CV or cover letter yet. Downgrade keeps resumes (nothing deleted); PDF downloads/cover letters/Live Resume/Fair View need Premium again.
- "Prices show in your local currency where we support it (EUR otherwise) — exact amount confirmed at checkout." Referral: 50% off for a friend.

## Templates & content
- Templates "designed by HR experts and optimized for ATS"; **all templates on every plan including Free** (Executive, Minimalist, Creative shown; full library at /resume-templates).
- Resume-example pages: role definition, key skills ATS scan for, a full worked example (fictional person, real-shaped bullets with numbers), and tips; "use it as a structure to copy, not as text to copy."

## Positioning / objections (site's own comparison table)
- **vs ChatGPT** — ChatGPT fine for wording a few lines; CopilotResume if you want the finished resume: ATS-safe templates, score vs the real job ad with missing keywords, one-click PDF.
- **vs Zety** — Zety fine if you already have a working resume there; CopilotResume if you want EU data storage (never sold, never used to train AI) and 16 supported languages.
- **vs resume.io** — resume.io fine if their plan suits you better; CopilotResume: build and check free, then $7 day pass / $15 30-day once (nothing renews) / $12 a month.
- **vs Kickresume / FlowCV** — those fine if you already have a resume you love; CopilotResume: AI that sharpens your real experience and never invents any, Darpan recruiter read, true two-column layouts, country-specific designs, free template/layout control.
- **Honest weak spot (stated on site):** the Job Tracker "is built for a laptop or desktop screen" — a phone-first tracker suits phone-only users better.
- Comparison caveat: "We only describe ourselves; other companies change their plans too often for us to speak for them."

## Specifics for answers
- Data/privacy: files "stored in the EU, never used to train AI"; cookies only for login/preference (theme, template, draft); "We do not sell your data or build profiles on you."
- Languages: "a toolkit that works in your language: 16 are supported" (site claim in comparison table).
- Country pages: Canada, Canada (FR) /cv-canadien, Germany, India, Netherlands, Nederland (NL), Philippines, South Africa.
- Other product pages linked (not fully crawled): How Our ATS Score Works, Secure Resume Builder, Honest Resume, Gender-Neutral Resume (Fair View), JSON Resume, legal hub / legal/refund-policy.
- Free start: /start; sign-in: /signin; no phone app mentioned.

## Contacts
- Support: **support@copilotresume.io** · Trustpilot: trustpilot.com/review/copilotresume.io
- ETLDataCompany B.V., Den Haag, The Netherlands · KVK: 87585413 · BTW: NL864338880B01
- Per the Connectors WhatsApp group CSV (not stated on the site): WhatsApp "Mayank Garg" (222762824126625@lid), LinkedIn maygarg/ (CSV tagline also cites "622 users, 20 paying customers" — not stated on the site).

# Deepshi — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**Deepshi (deepshi.ai)** is a private, unrestricted ("uncensored") AI platform from **Evermind Labs, Inc.** — one interface for chat, image, video, music and code, with a privacy architecture that stores your chats **locally on your device** rather than on Deepshi servers. Tagline: "Where AI meets freedom… Experience unrestricted intelligence with complete privacy." The site's claim: "**The only AI with third-party privacy verification**" (verified by Assured Information Solutions).

**One line for different audiences:**
- Privacy-conscious users: "Free to try with no account; conversations stored only on your device, not Deepshi's servers; independently verified."
- Power users / prosumers: "One subscription replaces ChatGPT + Claude + Gemini + image/video/music tools; Plus $19/mo, Pro $99/mo."
- Developers: "OpenAI-compatible API — Deepshi API access 100 req/min (Plus) and 500 req/min (Pro)."
- Writers / roleplay / creative: "Unfiltered native models (Deepshi Flash 2.0 / Deepshi Pro 3.0) plus AI characters, voice chat and a social feed."

## How it works
- **One chat interface**: write, generate images, produce videos, create music, and write/run code without switching tools.
- **Local-first privacy**: requests go to a proxy → a pool of GPUs across decentralized providers → response streamed back to your browser, **not persisted on Deepshi storage**; conversation history is kept in your local browser storage, encrypted (XSalsa20-Poly1305 / NaCl secretbox for chats; AES-GCM for saved images/videos).
- **Models**: built by Evermind Labs — **Deepshi Flash 2.0** (instant, everyday) and **Deepshi Pro 3.0** (deep reasoning/research); paid tiers add access to mainstream frontier models "including GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, Nano Banana, Sora, Google Veo + more."
- **Features**: AI characters (pre-edited + user-generated with earning potential), interactive voice chat (named voices: Companion, Maya, Spruce, Annie, Hannah, Trevor, Narrator), image/video/music generation, API access, cross-device sync (paid), social feed for generated media.
- **No account needed for free tier**: "Try for free. No sign up required." (at /chat).

## Key figures (site claims, 2026-10-18 crawl)
- "Over **70% of AI users** say censorship limits creativity" (homepage framing stat).
- Free tier: **30 messages daily** (first 5 at Deepshi Pro-level quality), **5 image generations daily**, never expires, no account/email.
- Plus: **$19/month** (still labeled "Deepershi plan" in some blog text), **1,200 multimedia credits** one-time.
- Pro: **$99/month**, **6,000 multimedia credits** one-time.
- Annual subscriptions: **save 20%**.
- Company: **Evermind Labs, Inc.**, "Copyright © 2026 Evermind Labs, Inc."
- Third-party privacy verification: **Assured Information Solutions**.

## Pricing (as displayed on /pricing and homepage, 2026-10-18)
| Plan | Price | Highlights |
|---|---|---|
| **Deepshi** | **$0 / forever** | 30 msgs/day (first 5 Pro-level), 5 images/day, smart reasoning + basic web search for citations, AI characters, post to feed; "your data is never used for training" |
| **Deepshi Plus** ("Most value") | **$19 / month** | Faster responses, expanded limits; top third-party models (Claude Opus, GPT-5.2, and more); Deep Research; create/customize characters; 1 free video/day; 10 free music/day; one-time 1,200 multimedia credits; encrypted cross-device sync + local or Cloud Vault backup; API 100 req/min |
| **Deepshi Pro** | **$99 / month** | Everything unlimited (messages, images, Deep Research, character creation), unlimited uploads/document+image analysis, fastest VIP processing, 5 videos/day, 30 music/day, 6,000 multimedia credits, early access + priority support, API 500 req/min |
- "Save 20% on annual subscriptions." · "Secure payment method." Upgrade/downgrade/cancel anytime, no long-term commitments.

# DesignLoop — distilled knowledge (from the website as of 2026-10-19)

## What it is (30 seconds)
**DesignLoop is a client website-feedback tool for agencies and freelancers.** The owner creates a review link for a website (or PDF); the client opens it and leaves comments pinned to the exact spot on the page — no account, no extension. Each request keeps the original screenshot, device size and suggested replacement copy. The owner then hands selected requests to their coding tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex — via copy, AI link or MCP), checks the returned proof on a private Implementation board, and only the owner can mark a request complete.

**One line for different audiences:**
- Agency/freelancer: "One review link replaces the email/chat/screenshot mess — and requests go straight to your coding agent, but you keep final approval."
- Client (guest reviewer): "Open the link, click what you want changed, suggest the exact wording — no account needed."
- Founder/dev using coding agents: "Your agent implements agreed client requests and submits proof; you approve before anything is closed."

## How it works (the review loop)
1. **Create a review** — add the website URL, start a named feedback round.
2. **Share one link** — the client browses the site (even at phone width), selects an area or text, comments, can suggest replacement copy (Copy mode → Suggest), request removal (Strike), and attach reference images.
3. **Hand off** — the owner sends agreed requests to Claude Code, Cursor or Codex: Copy for AI (one request), Copy AI link (whole current round; tool must support reading links), or Connect the review via MCP (private progress + submitted screenshots return to DesignLoop).
4. **Review and approve** — the Implementation board shows progress and submitted proof (private to the owner); the owner compares against the original request (Compare view: original screenshot beside the current result), asks for another pass if needed, and marks items "Approve and mark implemented". Clients see statuses; they never see owner notes or implementation activity.
5. **Rounds** — each review has named versions: one open for new comments, closed rounds stay as read-only history. Topics, contributor filters and bulk status updates are available.

## Key figures (website, with dates, as of 2026-10-19)
- Pricing: **Freelancer $19/mo ($190/yr) — 5 active projects; Studio $39/mo ($390/yr) — 15; Business $99/mo ($990/yr) — 50**. All plans: unlimited guest reviewers, unlimited feedback rounds, coding tool handoff, before/after comparisons.
- **7-day free trial**, starts with the first project, **no card required**; existing feedback stays readable after the trial.
- PDF reviews: PDFs **≤ 20 MB**. Submitted changes: up to **3 screenshots** (PNG/JPEG/WebP, ≤ 5 MB each).
- Guests always review for free; finished projects can be archived to free active-project slots.
- Site copyright: © 2026 DesignLoop. No customer/user counters published.

## Three audiences and what each gets

### Agency / freelancer / small team (owner)
- One review link per project; clients comment on the page itself; the original screenshot stays with the request even after the site changes.
- Active/History views, named rounds, topics, contributor filters, bulk status changes, reopen for another pass.
- Website reviews and PDF reviews in the same project list (same Active/History, versions, approval flow).
- Before-and-after comparison for every change; the client request stays open until the owner approves.
- Checklists for verifying changes (copy, images, layout, buttons, menus/forms, removed content) on the same device size as the original request.

### Client / guest reviewer
- Opens the shared link, identifies as a guest, comments — **no account, no extension, always free**.
- Can select text and suggest exact replacement copy, pin numbered comments to elements, review at phone width (device size captured), attach reference images.

### Developer / founder with a coding agent
- Three handoff options: Copy for AI, Copy AI link, MCP connection (named project token per review, or account-level connection via ChatGPT/custom MCP at mcp.designloop.ai/mcp with OAuth).
- Claude Code / Cursor / Codex each have a step-by-step workflow guide: connect → list active feedback to confirm the right review → make the agreed changes → submit with screenshots → owner approves on the Implementation board.
- Permissions: one-review connections (that review's feedback + private owner notes + implementation activity) vs account connections (all reviews you own + can create website/PDF reviews); revocable from the review or dashboard Connections page. **A connection never grants publishing access to the website.**

## Positioning (objections from the site)
- **Vs. screenshot markup / browser extensions / installed widgets:** DesignLoop is a shared review link — nothing for the client to install, comments stay connected to the page area, and the original screenshot survives site changes (the site compares these four annotation methods in a table on /website-annotation-tool).
- **"Do AI changes go live automatically?"** No. DesignLoop is a place to review implementation proof before marking feedback complete; publishing is controlled by the permissions and workflow in your coding tool — a DesignLoop connection does not grant access to the publishing account.
- **"Can the agent mark things done itself?"** No — only the project owner can approve and mark a client request implemented; agents return progress and proof privately.
- **Staging sites:** yes, when the staging URL is publicly reachable; sites behind private networks or logins may need another setup.

## Specifics for answers
- Clients never need an account; anyone with a shared link can view the review and comment as a guest.
- Works on public websites incl. Webflow and WordPress builds, plus coding-tool-built sites; the coding tool needs access to the site's source project to implement changes.
- PDF reviews: page comments, selected text, suggested replacement text, image attachments.
- MCP endpoint: https://mcp.designloop.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth; ChatGPT connection needs Developer mode; consent grants access to reviews you own incl. private notes and implementation activity; revoke via Connections).
- ChatGPT can create website/PDF feedback links, find a review, and summarize current-round feedback.
- Trial: 7 days from first project, no card; the trial is also started when connecting an MCP client that creates a first review.
- Pricing page/FAQ do not exist as separate URLs — they are homepage anchors (#pricing, #faq); /about, /contact etc. return errors.

## Contacts
- No public email or support channel is listed on the site. Start free / sign in: https://app.designloop.ai/login
- Site guides are authored "By Vince" (matches the Connectors WhatsApp contact Vince, lid 120736429637646@lid).
